This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency that would make the desktop/mobile `.name` color lighter in light theme than the base styling, but it’s a styling/design mismatch rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:239 — badge pill background flipped from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) but the paired &[href] { color: $secondary; } rule was not updated; in dark schemes linked badges render dark text on a dark-gray pill (contrast/unreadability regression) and need a dark-light-choose text color, as done in the second hunk around line 285

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss`, the pill `background-color` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, but the linked state still forces `&[href] { color: $secondary; }` unchanged. From the diff alone we can verify that in the dark choice the background is derived from `$secondary` while the text is also exactly `$secondary`, making a same-base color pairing likely to reduce contrast; nearby, a similar linked color rule *was* updated to `dark-light-choose(...)` (second hunk), supporting that this is an omission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — light-theme value changed 30% → 70% and the pair got swapped; the bold link goes from dark muted gray to ~L74% gray on white (contrast ≈ 2:1, well below readable), wrong relative to both the original and the PR's X% → (100−X)% convention
matched_golden_ids: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the light theme’s $lightness value is incorrect due to using/swapping 30% vs 70%, resulting in unintended text darkness/contrast changes. Although the candidate describes the direction as a swap, it still identifies the 30%/70% light-theme lightness mistake the golden comment highlights.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/modal.scss:101 — light value inverted 70% → 30%; the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:91, .custom-message-length) correctly keeps 70%/30%, so mobile now renders a visibly darker hint text than desktop in light mode

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `mobile/modal.scss` `.custom-message-length` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which makes the light-theme (primary) value 30% instead of 70%. In `desktop/modal.scss`, the analogous rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This is a clear inversion/inconsistency introduced by the diff and would plausibly render the mobile hint text much darker than desktop in light mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — light value changed 20% → 50%; the desktop equivalent (desktop/topic-post.scss:318, same h3) correctly keeps 20%/80%, so the mobile heading is now much dimmer than desktop in light mode

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `mobile/topic-post.scss` for `a.star h3` changing from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, i.e. the light-mode lightness component changes 20% → 50%. In the same PR, the desktop equivalent `desktop/topic-post.scss` keeps the 20%/80% pairing (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). This creates a verifiable regression/inconsistency in mobile styling relative to prior behavior and the desktop version, likely reducing contrast in light mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/user.scss:522 — .name light value changed 30% → 50%; possibly deliberate harmonization with adjacent .title (50%) but it is an unmentioned light-theme visual change in a PR scoped to dark-scheme fixes

adjudication.rationale: The diff in app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss changes `.name` color from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which is a light-theme visual change (30% → 50%) beyond simply adding dark/light selection. This is verifiable in the diff and could be unintended scope creep if the PR goal was only dark-scheme fixes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/user.scss:497 — same .name 30% → 50% light-theme value change as desktop/user.scss:522, undocumented in the PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `.name` in both `desktop/user.scss` and `mobile/user.scss` changing from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, i.e., the light-theme lightness value changes 30%→50%. However, the finding’s asserted issue (“undocumented in the PR”) cannot be verified from the diff, and the diff provides no evidence that this 30%→50% adjustment is incorrect vs. an intentional part of the broader dark/light theming changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Systemic duplication: the pattern dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - X%)) is hand-expanded at ~110 call sites across 31 files with the dark value implicitly coupled to the light value (Y = 100 − X) maintained by hand; this caused the five transcription slips and a one-line SCSS helper function (muted-color($pct)) would eliminate the entire failure class

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows many manual replacements of `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: Y%))`, where `Y` is often the hand-maintained complement (e.g. 40/60, 75/25, 80/20) across many files/lines. It’s also verifiable that some new call sites deviate from the apparent intended pairing or prior value (e.g. `desktop/topic-post.scss` changes `a` from primary 30% to `dark-light-choose(... primary 70%, secondary 30%)`; `mobile/modal.scss` changes `custom-message-length` from primary 70% to `dark-light-choose(... primary 30%, secondary 70%)`; `mobile/topic-post.scss` h3 switches from 20% to 50/50), illustrating the maintenance risk the finding describes. The suggested helper is an architectural/maintainability improvement rather than a directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/compose.scss:~177 — incomplete coverage: the PR fixes dark-scheme rendering of #reply-title:disabled and .wmd-input:disabled backgrounds in this block but leaves the adjacent color: darken($primary, 40%) untouched, yielding mid-gray input text in dark scheme where near-white-on-dark is intended (pre-existing, same bug class the PR exists to fix)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss`, the diff updates the disabled backgrounds for `#reply-title:disabled` and `.wmd-input:disabled` to use `dark-light-choose(...)`, but the adjacent `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` line remains unchanged in the same block. Given the PR’s broad theme of replacing `scale-color($primary, ...)` with `dark-light-choose(...)` for dark-scheme compatibility, leaving this text color as a single-scheme derivation is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in coverage (though the specific “near-white intended” claim can’t be proven from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Light-theme value swapped with dark value in desktop/topic-post.scss (~291, a bold link rule): light branch changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70%, washing out bold links to ~1.9:1 contrast on white in light themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`, the diff changes a bold link color from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Across the rest of the diff, the consistent pattern for `dark-light-choose(light, dark)` is `($primary, lower lightness)` for light themes and `($secondary, higher lightness)` for dark themes (e.g., `$primary 30%` / `$secondary 70%`). This specific change appears inverted (light branch uses `$primary 70%`, dark branch uses `$secondary 30%`), plausibly washing out the link color in light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Light-theme heading dimmed in mobile/topic-post.scss (~183, h3): light branch changed from 20% to 50%, inconsistent with the desktop h3 which correctly preserved 20%, causing mobile light-theme headings to render mid-gray

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss within `a.star h3`, the color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, so the light-theme branch is no longer 20% lightness. The analogous desktop rule in desktop/topic-post.scss preserves 20% for the light-theme branch (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), ...)`). This is a verifiable inconsistency introduced by the diff that would change mobile light-theme heading appearance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Light-theme value swapped in mobile/modal.scss (~103, .custom-message-length): light branch changed from 70% to 30%, exactly inverted compared to the identical desktop modal rule which correctly kept light 70% / dark 30%

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`, which inverts the usual light/dark mapping used throughout the diff (and specifically disagrees with `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` where the same selector uses `dark-light-choose(...70%..., ...30%...)`). This makes the mobile modal hint color inconsistent and likely incorrect for one of the themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Profile .name dimmed in light themes in desktop/user.scss (~523): light branch changed from 30% to 50%, making it identical to the adjacent .title rule and noticeably lighter in light themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss`, the `.name` rule’s light-theme color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, which is lighter and now matches the adjacent `.title` rule’s light branch (`...$lightness: 50%`). This is a concrete, diff-introduced visual regression/inconsistency (most other replacements preserve the original `$primary` lightness), making the finding verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Profile .name dimmed in light themes in mobile/user.scss (~498): same 30% to 50% light-branch change as the desktop .name rule, an unintended light-theme regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the mobile profile header `.name` color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (mobile/user.scss), matching a similar change in desktop/user.scss. This does alter the light-theme branch (30% -> 50% lightness), which could reduce contrast/dim the name in light themes, but the diff alone can’t prove it’s an unintended regression vs an intentional theming adjustment.
